\par\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\scriptsize\raggedright
"$\pm$ 0": std below 1e-08 of the mean (numerical noise; fixed test set and deterministic fit), not exactly zero.\par
SymGWR-T = degree-5 polynomial + k=1 nearest-reference Taylor surrogate (\texttt{SymGWR} in the CSVs); SymGWR-R = residual-anchored variant (\texttt{residual\_anchored}, from taylor\_variants\_accuracy\_per\_seed.csv).\par
(i) Random: 10 random 60/20/20 resamples; test sets overlap, pairs not strictly independent\par
(ii) Temp.-band: test set fixed (1,568 rows, same for every seed); only train/val partition varies\par
(iii) Comp.-group: 5 folds x 2 shuffles: test fold = seed \% 5, so 5 distinct test sets, each seen twice\par
(a) train rows capped at 2500 (random subsample, seed-dependent); val rows added on refit\par
(b) temperature column moved to index 0 before train\_pinn: the library physics loss penalises dG/d(feature 0), and feature 0 in the data is Mass\_fraction\_Nb\par
(c) GP protocol: alpha tuned on a 1000-row train subsample (val MSE), then ONE refit on train (capped 2500) + val; 25 min timeout\par
Seeds per method: 10; timeouts: 0, errors: 0.\par
\end{minipage}

\par\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\scriptsize\raggedright
Fit design rank 95 of 1286 polynomial terms (centred, bias-free), all 10 seeds; the minimum-norm solution sets the unconstrained part to zero.\par
Composition-axis accuracy holds for own-axis derivatives on the sweep lines only; cross-element, Ni and interior-composition gradients are not identified by the data.\par
Second derivatives: pure and d/dT-mixed on the own plane identified (null $\le$ 6.0e-13); cross-element mixed terms not identified (null 0.91--1.00).\par
Held-out = FD points whose centre row is not in that seed's train+val. A random row split keeps fit neighbours in the same (T, c) plane, so this is an interpolation test, not a held-out-composition test.\par
\end{minipage}

\par\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\scriptsize\raggedright
SymGWR-T extrapolates linearly from the nearest reference, so value and gradient both jump at cell boundaries. SymGWR-R adds a constant offset to the polynomial P, so its gradient (grad P) is continuous (jumps are zero up to rounding) and only the value jumps.\par
Not available: SymGWR-R-IDW is not a variant in continuity\_summary.csv (run\_continuity\_audit.py currently covers SymGWR-T, SymGWR-R only).\par
Switches = nearest-reference switches located by bisection and evaluated on both sides, summed over seeds; tie-plane switches excluded: 0.\par
\end{minipage}
\end{table*}
